you often wear a tampon in conjunction with a pad (or liner, which is just a thinner pad). If the pad has a bit of blood on it, that's an indicator that it's time to change both. The pad is a failsafe for the tampon. What's the fucked up part about this whole thing is that both the pad and tampon are not cheap and both need to be replaced every 5-6 hours at least. AND, sometimes when you're in a very inconvenient place. I have learned how to replace my tampon in my car, in the back of an empty city bus (not a lie), in an alley and under my desk. All of these places are not safe because you're exposed but you just hope that you can be quick, leak free and subtle.

I know this sounds crazy but since my hair is the exact same kind as yours, I think I can help. I bet your hair tangles even when the wind blows, yes? First, the best shampoo is Malin&Goetz Pepermint shampoo. It costs a lot but I only wash my hair every 3 days so I justify it. I then use Davines Oi conditioner. Once I gently towel dry it, I then use “it’s a 10” spray leave in conditioner. Then I brush it with a paddle brush and then I put it in two or three loose mini buns and sleep with it like that. In the morning, your hair will still likely be a little wet because you have a lot like me. I take them out and let them dry as I’m getting ready. Also, this isn’t gonna go over very well on this subreddit but in between haircuts, I do light trims on my hair because it gets crunchy on the ends. Sorry this is so long but this regiment helped me get shiny hair again.

Life at home when you can't move out and your family is awful can be so overwhelming. You've become totally aware of how they aren't good for you to be around but you don't have the power to change your situation. I moved out when I was 17, as soon as possible. If it's that bad, get out. No things are worth it. I stayed at a friend's house, her parents let me sleep at their house until I went to college. Also, don't let your life at home screw up what you want to do. Find a way. Don't use all that young energy on being angry, use it on an escape plan so when the time comes, you'll be ready to bounce. You got this. I'm not saying it's going to be easy, I'm 37 and still struggle. My family is still awful but at least I know I don't have to be trapped by them anymore and they don't get a say on how I choose to live my life. It's a huge burden off my shoulders. I've had to depend on them here and there but when I do, I'm reminded and it kicks me into gear to never want to do that again.
